kicker: IT services · growth in clients' currencies vs in rupees, Q2 FY27
title: The weak rupee did more for IT growth than clients did
dek: At five of six IT firms the currency added more to Q2 rupee revenue growth than client demand did (median 8.4 points). The rupee hit a seven-month high on 20 Nov, so that lift is shrinking.

hero.label: Median lift from the rupee
hero.note: Rupee growth minus constant-currency growth, Q2 FY27 year on year

read: Underlying demand is low single digits at the largest firms; with the rupee firmer, rupee growth will now lean on real volume.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 earnings calls; rupee: HDFC Sky, 20 Nov 2026
notes: Constant-currency growth (revenue at last year's exchange rates) and rupee revenue growth are as stated by each company on its Q2 FY27 call; the gap is rupee growth minus constant-currency growth, which mostly reflects the rupee's fall against the dollar, euro and pound over the year. Persistent reports dollar growth (+20%) rather than constant currency, so its gap also includes cross-currency moves. Wipro, Infosys and HCLTech gave constant-currency growth but no rupee growth in the call data, so they appear only in the panel; TCS grew 2.8% in constant currency and 11.2% in rupees. News hook: the rupee closed at 92.67 a dollar on 20 Nov 2026, a seven-month high and its fifth straight gain, on record foreign inflows (HDFC Sky, 20 Nov 2026); the Nifty IT index fell 3.1% in the week to 13 Nov (Liquide, 13 Nov 2026). Caveat: hedging gains and losses sit below revenue, so a firmer rupee affects margins with a lag that varies by firm.
